title: AI in Tax Research: What Every CPA Needs to Know
summary: AI tax research is the use of AI trained on primary tax authority, the Internal Revenue Code, Treasury Regulations, rulings, and case law, to answer complex tax questions in minutes, with citations you can verify against the source.
body_text: AI tax research is the use of AI trained on primary tax authority, the Internal Revenue Code, Treasury Regulations, rulings, and case law, to answer complex tax questions in minutes, with citations you can verify against the source. On platforms like TaxGPT, the research doesn't stop at the answer: the cited analysis flows into the client memo, the position on the return, and the review that follows. This guide covers how AI tax research works, where it actually saves time in your workflow, where research-only tools fall short, and how to evaluate one before your firm commits. What Is AI Tax Research? AI tax research applies purpose-built artificial intelligence to tax questions and returns answers grounded in primary authority (statutes, regulations, revenue rulings, private letter rulings, and court decisions) with a citation trail a professional can check. Unlike a general chatbot , it stays current as the law changes and shows its sources rather than asking for your trust. The authority layer is what separates the category from generic AI. A serious tool reads the IRC, Treasury Regulations, IRS rulings and notices, federal case law, state and local codes. The best coverage extends further, to territorial rules, U.S. tax treaties, and Canadian authority (the Income Tax Act, CRA guidance, and provincial rules) for firms with cross-border clients. When you ask whether a client’s remote employees create nexus, or how IRC § 174 capitalization interacts with a state that hasn’t conformed, the answer arrives with the sections and rulings that support it. One scoping point matters before you evaluate anything: research is where the engagement starts, not where the tool should stop. The question behind most research requests is never “find me an answer.” It’s “can we take this position, and what do we do about it?” Modern tax platforms treat the cited answer as the first artifact in a chain that includes the memo, the return, and the review. Research-only tools treat it as the finish line. Both designs exist in 2026, and knowing which one you’re buying is most of the evaluation. General AI vs. Research-Only AI vs. Tax Platforms Most buying mistakes in this category come from comparing tools that belong to different species. “AI tax research” gets used to describe three different things, and they behave differently the day a client’s money is on the line: General AI Chatbot Research-Only AI Tool AI Tax Platform Knowledge sources Open-web training data; no tax-specific grounding Curated primary tax authority Curated primary tax authority, U.S. and Canada. Citations Often missing or fabricated Linked to the underlying source Linked to the underlying source Currency Frozen at training time Updated as law changes Updated as law changes Jurisdictions Unreliable everywhere Typically federal + state Federal, state, local, territorial, and treaty After the answer Nothing: copy, paste, hope Some draft memos; the return, review, and client record stay outside The answer flows into memos, prep, review, and planning in place Client context None None; each session starts fresh Persistent client profiles carry facts across engagements Security Prompts may train the model Varies; check the attestation SOC 2 Type II, PII redaction, no training on client data Best for Brainstorming, never client work Firms that only need faster answers Firms automating the work around the answer too The first column is the easy call: a consumer chatbot will hand you a confident answer with a citation that doesn’t exist, and the hidden costs of ChatGPT wrappers compound from there. (If you want the full head-to-head, see TaxGPT vs ChatGPT .) The harder call is between the second and third columns, because on a demo they look identical: both answer a federal question quickly, with real citations. The difference only shows up after the demo, in the fourth row of that table, where the answer either becomes a work product or becomes your re-keying job. Where AI Accelerates the Five Steps of Tax Research Our complete guide to tax research walks through the five-step methodology in full: establish the facts, identify the issues, locate authority, evaluate and conclude, communicate. Here is where AI compresses each step, and where it doesn’t. Step 1: Establish the facts The facts rarely arrive as a tidy narrative. They arrive as a shoebox: prior-year returns, a brokerage statement, three Forms K-1, and a client email that contradicts one of them. AI document analysis reads the pile and surfaces what’s tax-relevant (entity structures, basis figures, state footprints, elections already made) so you start the research knowing what you’re actually researching. The common tax research challenges practitioners report almost always begin here, before a single authority gets pulled. Step 2: Identify the issues A client question is rarely one question. “Can I deduct this?” unpacks into character, timing, limitation, and jurisdiction issues. AI decomposes a multi-part fact pattern into the discrete issues it raises, including the one you might not have flagged at 6 p.m. in March, like a state conformity mismatch hiding under a routine federal question. Step 3: Locate authority This is the step AI compresses hardest: the difference between an afternoon in a research database and a few minutes with a cited answer. Ask in plain language, get the controlling sections, the relevant rulings, and the cases that matter, each linked to its source. The compression matters most on questions that cross jurisdictions. Take the IRC § 174 example from earlier: the federal answer is only the beginning, because a dozen states decoupled from the federal treatment and a client with a multi-state footprint needs the conformity picture state by state. Assembling that manually means a separate search per state. Asked well, AI returns the map in one pass, and a multi-jurisdiction grid like TaxGPT Matrix turns it into a table you can drop into workpapers. Speed here isn’t about impatience. Research time is mostly non-billable, and every hour it consumes during filing season comes out of review or advisory work that clients actually pay for. Step 4: Evaluate and conclude AI accelerates this step but does not perform it. What it does well: surface conflicting authority instead of hiding it, show the strength of support on each side, and lay out the reasoning path so you can follow it to the source. What stays yours: weighing the authority against your client’s facts, resolving the conflict, and owning the conclusion. Defensible tax research isn’t research a machine agreed with; it’s research a professional can stand behind, source by source. Step 5: Communicate the conclusion The classic time leak: the research is done, and now you rebuild it in a Word document, copying citations, restructuring the analysis, hoping nothing breaks in transit. On a platform, the cited research becomes the first draft of the memo or the client email, with the authorities still attached. This is also the step where the categories from the table above quietly separate: most research-only tools end at step 3 or 4, and the stronger ones will draft the memo. What none of them touch is what comes next: the return, the review, and the client record. Where Research-Only AI Tools Stop Take a question every growing firm has fielded since South Dakota v. Wayfair : an e-commerce client crossed economic nexus thresholds in three new states last year. A good research-only tool earns its keep here. Within minutes you have the three thresholds, the registration requirements, and the marketplace-facilitator rules, all cited. Now count what’s left. The client needs a memo they can act on, written, cited, and in plain English. The three state registrations trigger filing positions that have to land on actual returns. Those returns need review before they go out. The nexus finding reopens the entity-structure conversation the client has postponed twice. And every fact you established this season (the state footprint, the thresholds crossed, the positions taken) needs to be findable next season, when the same client adds two more states. With a research-only tool, the better ones will draft that memo for you. Everything after it, though, is an export, a re-key, a different tool, and a fresh context-setting session. On a platform, the same cited research drafts the memo, informs the return positions, feeds the completed-return review, and stays attached to the client’s profile for next year. The research took minutes either way. The engagement is where the two designs part company. To be fair to the category: several genuinely good research tools end at the answer by design. If answers are all your firm needs, they may serve you well. Knowing that before you buy is precisely the point of the next section. (Want to see the full chain on one of your own client questions? Book a demo and bring the fact pattern.)

(Nasdaq: KYIV; KYIVW), the parent company of JSC Kyivstar ("Kyivstar"), Ukraine's leading digital operator, today announced that Uklon, Ukraine's leading ride-hailing and delivery platform and part of Kyivstar's digital ecosystem, has closed a deal to acquire 100% of the operator e-Wings. The transaction was valued at UAH 97.6 million before adjustments. The acquisition deepens Kyivstar’s digital ecosystem strategy, adding a new mobility layer to a platform already used daily by millions of Ukrainians for transport, delivery, and payments. Uklon’s platform already spans ride-hailing, delivery, advertising, bus ticketing, and e-commerce, and now adds a new micromobility vertical, Uklon Scooters, to that portfolio. “Uklon’s acquisition of e-Wings is a clear example of how Kyivstar’s digital ecosystem strategy creates value beyond connectivity. By backing Uklon's move into micromobility, we are helping build a broader platform of digital services that meets more of our users’ everyday needs, while strengthening one of Ukraine's most dynamic digital businesses,” said Oleksandr Komarov, President of Kyivstar Group. “This deal is a milestone moment for Uklon: for the first time in our history, we are scaling through M&A, and we are doing so deliberately, choosing a direction that strengthens our digital ecosystem within the Kyivstar Group family of businesses. Uklon Scooters will become another touchpoint with users in daily urban mobility,” said Serhiy Hryshkov, CEO of Uklon. To lead the new business line, e-Wings co-founder Roman Motruk has been appointed Head of Micromobility, where he will drive the sector's strategic development and build synergies across Uklon’s broader ecosystem. Oleh Bilyi, e-Wings co-founder and former head of operations, becomes Head of Micromobility Operations, overseeing day-to-day operational processes. The unit will report to Vadym Ishchenko, Chief Operating Officer of Uklon, who leads growth of new products and services across the ecosystem. During the transition period, e-scooter rentals will continue to run through the existing e-Wings app across all 11 cities where the service operates. “Joining the Uklon ecosystem represents a fundamentally new level for our team. I am confident that combining our seven years of operational experience with Uklon’s powerful brand and resources will make moving around the city even more convenient for users,” said Roman Motruk, Head of Micromobility at Uklon. title: Wayfair Internship 2027–2028: Programs, Deadlines & How to Apply
summary: Wayfair's 2027–2028 internship guide: a paid 10-week Boston summer program ($40/hr for SWE), eligibility, the HackerRank interview loop, and how to apply.
body_text: Wayfair Internship 2027–2028: Programs, Deadlines & How to Apply Last updated: August 2026 Wayfair's software engineer interns earn $40 an hour, roughly $6,933 a month in Boston, with a $600 monthly housing stipend on some offers. That is about 17% above the US average for the role and among the higher intern rates for a non-FAANG e-commerce employer. The flagship 10-week summer program runs June through August at the company's Boston headquarters across engineering, data science, and business tracks, and it made the Yello x WayUp "Top 100 Intern Programs for 2025." Here is everything you need to know to land a Summer 2027 seat. Quick Facts Fact Detail Where to apply wayfair.com/careers (early-talent hub at aboutwayfair.com/careers/early-talent ). Each posting carries a Requisition ID (Summer 2026 SWE = 9848, Data Science = 9730) Application window (2027–28) Not yet published. Based on the Summer 2026 cycle (posted ~Sep 17, 2025), applications for summer 2027 are expected to open ~Sep–Oct 2026 and run through late 2026 / early 2027. Exact 2027 open/close dates NOT FOUND as of August 2026. Monitor wayfair.com/careers starting Fall 2026 Rolling? Partly. Early-talent applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with an "initial update within 3 weeks," but the flagship summer internship is a fixed, dated cohort (single summer start), not continuously open. Co-op roles run on two fixed intakes a year (Jan–June and July–Dec) Eligibility Pursuing a Bachelor's in CS or a related technical field (a quantitative discipline for data science), minimum 3.0 GPA, graduation within a ~9-month window after the internship (effectively rising seniors), and returning to school afterward Duration Summer internship: 10 weeks, June–August (Summer 2026 ran June 1 – Aug 7, 2026; summer 2027 expected ~early June to mid-Aug 2027). Co-op: 6 months. Early Leaders Program: 1-week immersion for second-year students Compensation SWE Intern: $40/hour (~$6,933/month in Boston, Summer 2025, with a $600/month housing stipend on some offers). Data Science Intern: $35/hour. Full-time SWE total comp ranges ~$125K–$257K+ across levels (community-labeled, Levels.fyi) Visa sponsorship Varies by role. The Data Science (Operations) intern JD explicitly does NOT sponsor (no STEM OPT EAD, H-1B, H-1B1, E-3, O-1, J-1, or TN). The SWE Intern JD states no sponsorship restriction. Confirm per posting Locations Boston, MA (4 Copley Place HQ). Hybrid: SWE interns are in-office 3 days/week (Tue–Thu), Data Science interns 4 days/week (Mon–Thu). Relocation to Boston for the summer is effectively required # Programs 8 "Early Talent" openings live as of Aug 2026, spanning Software Engineering, Data Science / Machine Learning, Business Analyst, Business Associate, Product Merchandising, the 6-month Co-op, and the 1-week Early Leaders Program Wayfair runs a fixed-cohort, 10-week paid summer internship in Boston (plus 6-month co-ops) across software engineering, data science, and business tracks. Summer 2027 postings are not live yet; based on the Summer 2026 cycle they are expected to open around Fall 2026. SWE interns are paid $40/hour, the interview loop centers on a HackerRank online assessment plus behavioral rounds on Wayfair's three People Principles, and interns are evaluated with the goal of a full-time return offer. Externships are short, remote projects where you finish real work for a real company. The Wayfair AI Agent Engineering Externship and the Beats by Dre Data Analytics Externship build the ship-real-code and data-to-insight evidence that Wayfair's technical assessment and case rounds reward. Explore all Externships . What Is a Wayfair Internship? A Wayfair internship is a paid, fixed-cohort summer program based at the company's Boston headquarters. Wayfair Inc. is one of the largest online retailers of furniture and home goods, founded in 2002 (as CSN Stores, rebranded Wayfair in 2011) by Niraj Shah and Steve Conine, publicly traded on the NYSE as W since its 2014 IPO, and reporting $12.46 billion in 2025 revenue with roughly 12,800 employees and a catalog of about 14 million items from 11,000-plus suppliers. The 10-week summer internship, which made the Yello x WayUp "Top 100 Intern Programs for 2025," spans engineering, data science, and business tracks. Interns own a real project end-to-end, work in a hybrid model out of the 4 Copley Place office, and are evaluated with the goal of a full-time return offer. Alongside the summer program, Wayfair runs 6-month co-ops (two intakes a year) and a 1-week Early Leaders Program for second-year students, so there is more than one on-ramp depending on where you are in school. When Do Wayfair Internship Applications Open for 2027–2028? Wayfair has not published a Summer 2027 timeline yet, so the dates below are expected, projected from the documented Summer 2026 cycle. That cycle's SWE and Data Science intern postings went live on job boards around September 17, 2025, roughly eight to nine months before the June start, so applications for summer 2027 are expected to open around September or October 2026. Once you apply, Wayfair says candidates receive an initial update within about three weeks, then move through a HackerRank online assessment, a technical phone screen, and a virtual onsite. The build window is now: sharpen SQL, Python, and object-oriented coding, finish a portfolio project you can walk through, and set alerts on wayfair.com/careers and aboutwayfair.com/careers/early-talent for Fall 2026. Now · Summer 2026 YOU ARE HERE Summer 2027 postings are not live yet. This is the build window: sharpen SQL, Python, and object-oriented coding, get comfortable using AI in your daily workflow (a listed Wayfair preference), and finish a portfolio project you can defend in a technical round. The Wayfair AI Agent Engineering Externship and the Beats by Dre Data Analytics Externship are remote, real-company projects that give you finished technical work to point at when Summer 2027 applications open. Summer to early Fall 2026 EXPECTED Prep window. Polish your resume around measurable project outcomes, practice LeetCode easy-to-medium array and string problems with hashmaps, and rehearse STAR-method stories mapped to Wayfair's three People Principles. Draft your "answer-first" behavioral responses now. ~Sep–Oct 2026 (expected) EXPECTED ROLLING — APPLY WEEK 1 Applications for summer 2027 are expected to open, based on the Summer 2026 postings that went live ~Sep 17, 2025. Because early-talent review is rolling with updates within ~3 weeks, apply in week one of the posting rather than waiting for a deadline. Winter 2026 to Spring 2027 (expected) EXPECTED Assessment and interview season: HackerRank online assessment, a ~45-minute technical phone screen, then a virtual onsite (typically one ~45-min technical plus one ~45-min behavioral, sometimes several back-to-back the same day). Offers are expected to land Winter–Spring 2027. Summer 2027 Expected internship window: ~10 weeks, roughly early June to mid-August 2027 (Summer 2026 ran June 1 – Aug 7). Hybrid in Boston, 3 in-office days for SWE and 4 for data science. Interns are evaluated with the goal of a full-time return offer after graduation. Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open Wayfair reviews early-talent applications on a rolling basis and tells candidates to expect an initial update within about three weeks, which means the pool is being read and cut as it fills, not all at once after a deadline. Combine that with a fixed-cohort summer program that has a set number of seats and the math is simple: applying in the first week of the posting puts you in front of a recruiter while the most slots are still open. Waiting is the single most avoidable mistake. Concretely, that means three things. First, have your resume and portfolio ready before Fall 2026 so you can submit the day the posting appears. Second, be prepared to move quickly into the HackerRank online assessment, because the technical screen follows fast once you clear application review. Third, line up your STAR-method behavioral stories in advance, structured around Wayfair's three People Principles, so the recruiter screen and hiring-manager round do not catch you flat. Set alerts on wayfair.com/careers and the aboutwayfair.com early-talent page now, and treat the moment 2027 postings go live as a race, not a window. Which Wayfair Internship Programs Should You Target? Wayfair's early-talent program spans several tracks under one summer umbrella, plus a longer co-op. The table below covers the tracks most relevant to a technical or quantitative candidate, drawn from the live Summer 2026 postings and the official intern-program page. Details reflect the Summer 2026 cycle; expect close equivalents for summer 2027. Program Focus Duration Key skills Software Engineering Intern Full project life-cycle work across teams like Global Supplier Tech, Supply Chain Retail Tech, and Customer Technology; individual and group projects 10 weeks (summer) Object-oriented programming (Java, C), Python, SQL, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, full-stack and/or mobile, big data and ML interest Data Science Intern (Operations) Multi-terabyte datasets (sales, clickstream, logistics); demand forecasting, product segmentation, network design, dashboards. No visa sponsorship for this role 10 weeks (summer) SQL (aggregate functions, joins), Python, Excel, Looker, Google Cloud (VertexAI, BigQuery, GCS), quantitative analysis Machine Learning Intern Listed as a technology-function intern track; overlaps heavily with the data science and software engineering tracks. Standalone 2026 ML-intern JD NOT FOUND 10 weeks (summer, est.) Python, big data, ML fundamentals, quantitative analysis on large datasets Business Analyst Intern Case-study-driven analysis across Commercial, Operations, Talent, and Finance sub-functions; business acumen and metrics focus 10 weeks (summer) Excel, data-driven decision-making, case analysis, communication, business metrics (conversion, AOV, margin) Business Associate Intern Operational and commercial project work across Commercial, Operations, and Talent sub-functions 10 weeks (summer) Analytical problem-solving, communication, project ownership, business acumen Co-op (rotational / extended) 6-month, full-time paid program in Boston with two intakes a year (Jan–June and July–Dec); open to undergrad, grad, and PhD depending on the role 6 months Track-dependent; e.g. Data Scientist Co-op mirrors the DS intern skill set at greater depth See current openings at wayfair.com/careers and the early-talent hub at aboutwayfair.com/careers/early-talent . If you are earlier in school, the 6-month co-op and the 1-week Early Leaders Program are lower-bar entry points than the rising-senior summer internship. What Are the Eligibility Requirements? Requirements below come from the live Summer 2026 SWE Intern (Req 9848) and Data Science Intern (Req 9730) job descriptions plus the official early-talent pages. Expect the same shape for summer 2027, with the graduation window shifting forward a year: • Degree: Currently pursuing a Bachelor's in Computer Science or a related technical field (Data Science, Analytics, Mathematics, Statistics, or another quantitative discipline for the DS track). For summer 2027, expect a graduation window of roughly December 2027 to August 2028. • GPA: Minimum 3.0, stated explicitly on both intern JDs. • Return-to-study: You must be returning to your course of study after the internship, which effectively targets rising seniors. • Commitment: 40 hours per week (roughly 9am–5pm, Mon–Fri) for the full 10-week program, hybrid out of the Boston office. • Work authorization: The Data Science (Operations) role explicitly does NOT sponsor (no STEM OPT EAD, H-1B, H-1B1, E-3, O-1, J-1, or TN). The SWE Intern JD states no sponsorship restriction. Confirm per posting. • AI fluency: Both JDs now list a "strong comfort level and appetite to use AI in daily workflow" as a preferred qualification. Who Is Wayfair's Summer Internship Actually For? The summer program is built for rising seniors. The SWE JD requires your degree to be conferred within a specific roughly nine-month window after the internship AND that you return to school afterward, which quietly rules out most graduating seniors and early-stage underclassmen. If you fall outside that window, the 6-month co-op is the better fit: it runs on Jan–June and July–Dec intakes and is open to a wider range, including grad and PhD students on some roles, while second-year students can start with the 1-week Early Leaders Program. Visa sponsorship is the other filter to check carefully, because it varies by role: the Data Science (Operations) intern posting states plainly that Wayfair will not sponsor, while the SWE Intern posting carries no such restriction. Read the specific requisition you are applying to rather than assuming the whole program behaves the same way. What Skills Does Wayfair Look For, and How Do You Build Them? Wayfair's two published intern JDs, the Summer 2026 Software Engineer Intern (Req 9848) and Data Science Intern (Req 9730), point to a consistent core: SQL, Python, and object-oriented programming show up in both, alongside an explicit expectation that you are comfortable using AI in your daily workflow. The SWE track adds front-end and full-stack breadth (JavaScript, HTML/CSS, mobile), while the data science track leans on Excel, Looker, and Google Cloud tooling for work on multi-terabyte datasets. Wayfair tests these through a HackerRank assessment and applied rounds rather than pure trivia, so the ability to write clean, working code and reason about data matters more than memorized algorithms. The chart below counts how many of the two official intern JDs list each skill. What Wayfair looks for in interns Skills across 2 Wayfair intern & analyst job descriptions · 2025–26 Wayfair Summer 2026 SWE + Data Science intern JDs, projecting the summer 2027 cycle SQL (joins, aggregate functions) 2 of 2 Python 2 of 2 Object-oriented programming (Java, C) 2 of 2 Big data & ML interest; analysis on large datasets 2 of 2 Comfort using AI in daily workflow 2 of 2 JavaScript + HTML/CSS (front-end) 1 of 2 Full-stack and/or mobile development 1 of 2 Excel + BI visualization (Looker) 1 of 2 Cloud tooling (VertexAI, BigQuery, GCS) 1 of 2 Method: full-text analysis of two official Wayfair intern job descriptions (SWE Intern Summer 2026 Req 9848; Data Science Intern Operations Summer 2026 Req 9730) plus the official early-talent pages. N=2 is a small sample, so counts show which skills are shared across both tracks versus track-specific, not a ranked market share. Soft skills (communication, project ownership, comfort with ambiguity) are evaluated in interviews but counted separately. How Is Demand for Software Engineering Interns Moving Right Now? Software engineering intern hiring right now: July 2026 Across US software-engineer-intern postings tracked this week · aggregate market data, all employers = About 637 US software-engineer-intern postings were open on July 11, holding near the ~650 tracked at the start of the month (654 on July 6) ★ ML pays a premium: machine-learning-intern postings advertise about $87,700 versus about $83,900 for general software-engineer-intern roles, which rewards the big-data and ML lean of Wayfair's data science track ▲ The bench you convert into is deep: 136,389 US software-engineer postings are open right now at roughly $164K mean advertised salary July 2026 is this tracker's baseline month, so month-over-month shifts show up at the August update. The signal today is level: intern demand is steady, and the ML-heavy end of it pays more, which favors candidates who can back a Wayfair data or SWE application with real quantitative work. Method: aggregate analysis of US software-engineer-intern, machine-learning-intern, and software-engineer postings via Adzuna / JSearch, July 2026 baseline. The sample indexes a fraction of all US postings, so figures show direction and relative level, not total market share. Build These Skills Before You Apply And the skills in that chart map cleanly to remote Externships where you finish a real project before Wayfair's 2027 postings even open. Skill (from real JDs) JD evidence Externship that builds it Full-stack & AI-systems engineering (SWE track) SWE JD: "OOP languages, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, Python," "full-stack and/or mobile," "appetite to use AI in daily workflow" Wayfair AI Agent Engineering SQL, Python & quantitative analysis on large datasets DS JD: "SQL aggregate functions and joins," "multi-terabyte datasets," "demand forecasting, dashboards" Beats by Dre Data Analytics Data-to-insight storytelling & business metrics Business/DS JDs: case studies on "conversion, AOV, margin," "data-driven decision-making," answer-first communication NASCAR Sports Analytics How close is the overlap? The Wayfair AI Agent project is applied engineering that yields the ship-real-code evidence a technical screen probes for, the Beats by Dre project builds the SQL-to-dashboard story the data science round wants, and the NASCAR project turns raw numbers into a recommendation, which is exactly what Wayfair's case-style rounds reward. What Is the Wayfair Application and Interview Process Like? Wayfair's early-talent hiring process combines a coding assessment with structured behavioral rounds. The steps below reflect the official interview-prep guidance plus community reports for the intern track: 1. Apply online at wayfair.com/careers (or via the aboutwayfair.com early-talent hub) when summer 2027 postings open, expected ~Fall 2026. Each posting has a Requisition ID (Summer 2026 SWE = 9848, Data Science = 9730). 2. Application review. Expect an initial update within about three weeks. Review is rolling, so apply early in the posting window. 3. Recruiter screen. A ~30-minute phone or video call covering your experience, motivation, and compensation, and setting up the technical assessment for tech roles. 4. Online assessment (HackerRank). A timed coding test, reported as LeetCode easy-to-medium (arrays and strings with a hashmap tweak). Business and data science versions add one or two business or case problems. 5. Technical phone screen. A ~45-minute video round with a coding problem plus a resume walkthrough. 6. Virtual onsite. Multiple back-to-back interviews, typically one ~45-minute technical and one ~45-minute behavioral; some candidates report roughly four ~30–45 minute interviews in a single day. 7. Final / hiring-manager round. A STAR-method behavioral conversation built on Wayfair's three People Principles ("We Win Together," "We Are Always Improving," "We Drive Results"), using an "answer-first" communication style. Business and data science tracks include a case-study interview. Two things to keep in mind. First, the coding bar is moderate, not FAANG-heavy: think clean array, string, and hashmap solutions rather than exotic algorithms. Second, behavioral performance carries real weight here, so prepare specific STAR stories mapped to the three People Principles and practice leading with your answer before the supporting detail. What Students on Reddit Say Three community threads give a first-hand look at Wayfair's intern hiring process, all paraphrased. The intern technical round was LeetCode easy-to-medium, arrays and strings with a hashmap twist, paired with a walk-through of your resume rather than anything exotic. r/developersIndia SWE intern interview, paraphrased · read the thread The loop was one ~45-minute technical phone screen followed by a virtual onsite that was essentially one 45-minute technical interview plus one 45-minute behavioral interview. r/csMajors internship interview prep, paraphrased · read the thread Expect four separate 30-to-45-minute interviews in a single day, with the behavioral rounds digging into your past experiences more than raw coding. r/boston onsite experience, paraphrased · read the thread How Do You Stand Out for a Wayfair Internship? Three moves, all executable before Summer 2027 postings open. First, prove you can ship, not just solve puzzles: a portfolio project in Python or a full-stack app you can walk through end-to-end speaks directly to the SWE track, and a SQL-and-dashboard analysis on a real dataset speaks to the data science track. Wayfair's technical screen and case rounds reward built work over memorized algorithms. Second, get fluent leading with the answer, because both the hiring-manager round and the case interviews use an "answer-first" structure on top of the STAR method, and candidates who bury the conclusion lose the room; rehearse three or four stories mapped to "We Win Together," "We Are Always Improving," and "We Drive Results." Third, show comfort using AI in your workflow, now a listed preference on both intern JDs, by pointing to a project where you used AI tooling to move faster and can explain the decisions you kept ownership of. Finish a remote Externship in the same problem space and you walk into the recruiter screen with finished, defensible work instead of a list of coursework. What Other Companies Should You Consider? Wayfair sits at the intersection of e-commerce, retail tech, and large-scale data. If you are building an internship list around that profile, these are the natural neighbors to apply to in parallel: Amazon The e-commerce and cloud giant with a far larger, more structured intern program and deep SWE, data, and operations tracks Guide → Chewy Online pet retailer with a comparable e-commerce engineering and analytics stack and a rising-senior summer program Careers site Williams-Sonoma Home and furnishings retailer with digital, supply-chain, and merchandising tech roles that overlap Wayfair's tracks Careers site Etsy Marketplace platform with strong data science and full-stack engineering internships in a two-sided commerce setting Careers site Overstock (Bed Bath & Beyond) Direct home-goods e-commerce competitor with engineering and analytics roles on a similar catalog-and-logistics problem set Careers site Our tech internships summer 2027 guide maps the whole landscape, timeline by timeline. FAQ Can I still apply for a summer 2026 Wayfair internship? No. The Summer 2026 program already ran (June 1 to August 7, 2026), so those postings are closed. Your target now is the Summer 2027 cycle. Based on the Summer 2026 postings that went live around September 17, 2025, expect Summer 2027 listings to open around Fall 2026. Set alerts on wayfair.com/careers and the aboutwayfair.com early-talent page so you can apply in the first week. Does Wayfair offer internships for 2027? Yes. Wayfair runs an annual 10-week summer internship (June to August, Boston) across engineering, data science, and business tracks, plus 6-month co-ops and a 1-week Early Leaders Program. Summer 2027 postings are not yet live as of August 2026; based on the Summer 2026 cycle, expect them to open around Fall 2026. Exact 2027 open and close dates are not yet published. How much do Wayfair interns get paid? Software Engineer Interns are paid $40/hour, about $6,933 a month in Boston for Summer 2025, with a $600/month housing stipend on some offers. Data Science Interns are paid $35/hour. Full-time SWE total compensation ranges from roughly $125K at entry to $257K-plus at higher levels (community-reported via Levels.fyi, not official). What are the eligibility requirements? A bachelor's in CS or a related technical field (or a quantitative discipline for data science), a minimum 3.0 GPA, graduation within a specific window after the internship (effectively rising seniors), and a commitment to return to school afterward. The Data Science (Operations) role does not offer visa sponsorship; the SWE Intern posting states no such restriction, so confirm per posting. How long is the program and where is it? The summer internship is 10 weeks (June 1 to August 7, 2026 for Summer 2026), based at Wayfair's Boston headquarters at 4 Copley Place. It is hybrid: SWE interns are in-office 3 days a week (Tue to Thu) and Data Science interns 4 days a week (Mon to Thu). Relocation to Boston for the summer is effectively required. What does the interview process look like? A recruiter screen, a HackerRank online assessment, a roughly 45-minute technical phone screen (LeetCode easy-to-medium), and a virtual onsite with technical and behavioral rounds, sometimes several back-to-back the same day. Behavioral questions follow Wayfair's three People Principles using the STAR method and an answer-first structure; business and data science tracks add a case-study interview. Which tech skills matter most? SQL, Python, and object-oriented programming appear across both intern JDs. The SWE track adds JavaScript, HTML/CSS, and full-stack or mobile experience; the data science track adds Excel, Looker, and Google Cloud tools (VertexAI, BigQuery, GCS). Comfort using AI in your daily workflow is now a listed preference on both roles. Do interns get return offers? Wayfair evaluates interns "with the goal of extending offers to rejoin full-time after graduation" and describes the internship as a preview of full-time work. A specific conversion percentage is not published, so treat conversion as a stated goal rather than a guaranteed rate. Wayfair's Summer 2027 seats are not posted yet, but the strongest applications are built months before the listing goes live. Spend the runway turning coursework into proof: a remote Externship gives you a finished, real-company project to point at the moment applications open in Fall 2026. About the Author Bifei Wang has spent 17 years focused on human flow and the growth of young professionals, spanning international education, career training and coaching, and recruitment process outsourcing. Over 7 years at Extern, he has had one-on-one sessions with thousands of students exploring careers in consulting, finance, tech, marketing, and data, giving him a firsthand view of how the job market has shifted for early-career professionals and what it actually takes to break in.

title: TD Asset Management Inc. expands its TD Target Maturity Bond ETFs lineup with new TD Target 2031 Investment Grade Bond Fund - ETF Series ("TBCK")
summary: TD Asset Management Inc. ("TDAM"), the manager of TD Exchange-Traded Funds (TD ETFs), has announced the launch of TD Target 2031 Investment Grade Bond Fund - ETF Series ("TBCK"), which begins...
body_text: TORONTO , Aug. 18, 2026 /CNW/ - TD Asset Management Inc. ("TDAM"), the manager of TD Exchange-Traded Funds (TD ETFs), has announced the launch of TD Target 2031 Investment Grade Bond Fund - ETF Series ("TBCK"), which begins trading today on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Part of the broader TD Target Maturity Bond ETFs suite, TBCK offers exposure to a portfolio of investment-grade Canadian corporate bonds denominated in Canadian dollars with a target maturity of 2031, supporting investors seeking a defined investment horizon. For investors, TBCK offers: A simple and efficient way to manage cash flows with the potential to earn an attractive yield from a diversified portfolio of investment-grade Canadian corporate bonds Ability to align maturity dates with cash needs, providing a streamlined way to help meet financial goals A convenient and cost-efficient solution, with a low management fee of 0.20%, that can be used within laddered bond strategies to help structure fixed income allocations across maturities "Our TD Target Maturity Bond ETFs are designed for investors seeking regular income and capital preservation, while benefiting from professional management and low costs," said Rachana Bhat, CFA, Vice President & Director, Lead of Credit Portfolio Management, TDAM. title: How Claude Code Changed Recruiting
summary: An autonomous ATS + CRM for executive search firms built for the age of AI.
body_text: AI has been in recruiting for a while now. Recruiters use ChatGPT to write outreach, summarize resumes, come up with interview questions. Helpful, but it doesn't change how the work gets done. You still do the task, you just have help writing it. Claude Code is a different thing. Not because the model is smarter. Because it writes and runs code on your own files. That sounds like a developer thing. It isn't. For a long time, if you wanted to pull every candidate you haven't contacted in six months and check them against your client list, you had two options. Find someone technical, or do it by hand in Excel over a weekend. There was no middle. Now you type what you want in plain English and it writes the script. That's the change. Not AI doing recruiting. Just the coding requirement going away. One thing worth saying before the examples. It's still code, and code does exactly what it was told, fast, across four thousand records. So work on an export instead of your live database, ask it to show you what it plans to change before it changes anything, and open a few records yourself to check. Takes five minutes and it's the difference between trying this and being scared of it. Here's what we're seeing firms actually do with it. Cleaning up the database Most firms know their database is dirty. Same person in there three times, titles all over the place, a lot of dead emails. The numbers back it up. Contact data decays about 2.1% a month, or 22.5% a year, based on the MarketingSherpa research HubSpot uses. Recruiting is worse than that because your whole database is people who change jobs for a living. On duplicates, most databases run 10% to 30%, and under 5% is what a well-run one looks like. That usually takes tooling and someone who owns it. Most firms have neither. Datamagnet So people are just writing the cleanup themselves now. Dedupe. The thing to know is don't match on name, or you'll merge two different Michael Chens and lose a relationship. Go in order: LinkedIn URL first since it's the only unique ID in recruiting data, then email, then name plus company as a fallback. Sort by confidence so the obvious ones merge and the murky ones go in a file you look at. The part people miss is what survives the merge. A guy who built a job tracking system with Claude Code ran into this and wrote up the fix. His rule keeps the row marked as applied when two records match, because just keeping the first row could erase the fact that he'd actually applied. Same thing in recruiting. If one duplicate has a screen note from 2024 and the other is a blank LinkedIn import, the blank one shouldn't win just because it's newer. You have to say that out loud or the script won't know. Titles and companies. VP Eng, VP of Engineering, and V.P., Engineering are one role and your filters treat them as three. Meta and Facebook are one company. Have it group the variants, show you the groups, pick the right version for each. Then keep the mapping file, so next month's import runs through it on the way in. Moving data around Sheets into the system. Everyone has longlists sitting in Google Sheets that never made it into the ATS. Built for a search, search closed, 300 qualified people stuck in a tab. Read the sheet, check each row against what's already in the system so you don't recreate duplicates, add what's new, tag it to the search. And back out. Pull the pipeline for a search, format it the way that client likes it, drop it in a sheet. Monday morning, without you doing it. The report your ATS won't give you. Time in stage by recruiter. Candidates sitting 30 days with nothing logged. Clients you haven't touched in 90 days. Every system has one report it can't do and you don't need your vendor to build it. Export the data, describe what you want, save it as a script, run it every Friday. The first time is usually rough. Blank owner fields on hundreds of records, jobs with no candidates attached, a quarter with no client activity logged. Better to know. Sourcing and everything after People who've been at this a few months aren't cleaning data anymore. Sourcing is the clearest one. It used to mean writing search strings, testing title variations, fixing filters, then doing it again for the next role. One recruiter described automating it: "I created a sourcing strategy, sub agent and then a sourcing subagent. It creates a sourcing strategy and then hands it off to the sourcing sub agent and brings back candidates for a search that I'm working on. This was a little more involved and I built it in OpenClaw using Claude Code." Others build around tools they already pay for : "Basically, when you publish a job in your DB, you get an email with the most suitable candidates from your ATS." Another runs Claude Code across Google Workspace , enrichment tools, and a CRM: "Claude can directly make you the spreadsheets... I push it to HubSpot or Attio and take it from there." Some went after research, which has always been limited by time not ideas. One set up a daily brief using Claude Code : "You wake up at 7 AM... important email you need to look at, your schedule/meetings... industry news, mergers and acquisitions in your industry, even new job openings at potential clients." The same idea can be applied to candidate management. By connecting Claude to your ATS, you can receive a prioritized morning brief covering candidates who need follow-up, stalled searches, upcoming offers, and other pipeline risks. We put together a step-by-step guide to automating a daily candidate pipeline brief with Claude . A recruiting leader described automating the routine layer of the job : "Sourcing. Pipelines. Outreach. Follow-ups. Scheduling. The work that quietly eats every recruiter's week." They said it gave each recruiter back more than ten hours a week. A Claude Code workspace, reusable skills, tools connected through MCPs and APIs, routines on a schedule. That connection piece is why we built the Stardex MCP server, since most of this falls apart if the data has to leave the system by copy-paste. What it adds up to Recruiters aren't turning into engineers. Nobody's learning data structures. But they're not just users of software anymore either. The coding requirement went away. What's left is knowing what you want and checking the work. The split isn't between recruiters who use AI and recruiters who don't. Everyone uses AI now. It's between recruiters whose knowledge sits in their head and recruiters whose knowledge sits in something that runs without them. Start with duplicates. It's an afternoon, you're working on a copy so the risk is low, and it teaches you the rest.

title: 2026 Toyota Prius Pricing, Specs, and Release Date
summary: Perhaps the best-known hybrid on the market, the Toyota Prius carries its sleek new style into 2026 along with available all-wheel drive and up to 57 mpg.
body_text: Toyota derived the Prius name from a Latin word meaning “to go before,” which is fitting because it was the world’s first mass-produced hybrid vehicle. Now in its fifth generation in the United States, the 2026 Toyota Prius offers more than just fuel efficiency. It’s more stylish and sporty than previous versions, offering buyers a zero-compromise take on modern transportation. And, of course, it’s extremely fuel efficient. 2026 Toyota Prius Pricing, Specs, and Release Date What’s New for the 2026 Toyota Prius Design Powertrain Interior Technology Safety Pricing and Release Date Further Research What’s New for the 2026 Toyota Prius The Toyota Prius rolls into the 2026 model year without any major changes. The Nightshade Edition that hit the market in 2025 remains on sale, with blacked-out elements inside and out and unique 19-inch wheels. Interestingly, the Prius Nightshade is offered in white and in an exclusive shade of yellow in addition to the usual black. Design Those who aren’t familiar with the current Prius, introduced in 2023, may remember Toyota’s previous dowdy or funky little hybrids. That’s no longer the case. Now in its 25th year on the U.S. market, the 2026 Toyota Prius has a sleek look, with a steeply raked windshield, sharp headlights, and a swept-back profile that looks both sporty and aerodynamic. Powertrain Prius models with front-wheel drive (FWD) feature a 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and electric motor that collectively produce 194 horsepower. With optional all-wheel drive (AWD), an additional electric motor powering the rear wheels increases total output to 196 hp. Toyota estimates that the FWD Prius will return up to 57 mpg in the city, 56 mpg on the highway, and 57 mpg combined. In XLE, Nightshade, and Limited trims, the FWD Prius drops to 52 mpg across the board due to larger 19-inch wheels instead of the base car’s 17-inch units. With AWD, the 2026 Prius is rated at 53 mpg city, 54 mpg highway, and 54 mpg combined, or 49 mpg city, 50 mpg highway, and 49 mpg combined in XLE, Nightshade, or Limited trims. All Prius models feature three selectable drive modes: Normal, an Eco mode that limits power to boost efficiency, and a Sport mode that quickens the throttle response. Interior The fourth-generation Prius adopted a more traditional interior design compared to previous versions, with a digital gauge cluster in front of the driver set into a trapezoidal housing. The main 8-inch touchscreen in the center of the dash is also in a trapezoid-shaped panel in LE, XLE, and Nightshade models, though the Limited gets a larger 12.3-inch screen with a more squared-off shape. Base LE models get cloth seating surfaces in black or gray, but all other Prius variants get a leatherette that Toyota calls SofTex. The rakish roofline means tall occupants may find headroom a little tight in both the front and rear seats, bu there's a good amount of legroom. Cargo space—23.8 cubic feet in base models and 20.3 cubic feet in all others—is also down slightly compared to the third-generation model, but still easily accessible due to the car's hatchback shape. Technology A digital gauge cluster and central touchscreen infotainment system are fitted to all 2026 Prius models. Only the Limited model gets a standard 12.3-inch display (the larger screen can be optioned on other models), while other versions come standard with a small 8-inch unit. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard across the board. Toyota’s latest infotainment software package is easy to use and, in addition to its touch-based menu, accepts voice commands. Prius Limited models feature an eight-speaker JBL audio system with an amplifier, while all other versions get a standard six-speaker system. Included in the package are automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, adaptive cruise control, lane-departure warning with steering assist, lane-keep assist, traffic-sign assist, high-beam assist, blind-spot monitors, rear cross-traffic alert, a safe-exit alert, and proactive driving assist (PDA). PDA uses information from the car’s camera and radar systems to brake or provide steering assist when the system deems it necessary. The 2026 Toyota Prius earned a Top Safety Pick+ award from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS). That’s the agency’s highest ranking, and means the Prius received the top Good score in the small overlap front, updated moderate overlap front, and updated side crashworthiness tests. The Prius also earned the maximum five-star overall safety rating from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). Pricing and Release Date At the time of writing, the 2026 Toyota Prius was on sale with a starting price of $30,050 (including destination). Adding AWD raises the base MSRP to $31,450. The XLE FWD model starts at $33,495, with the 12.3-inch infotainment screen costing an additional $735, while a fixed panoramic glass roof adds $1,000. The XLE AWD model starts at $34,895 and offers the same options as the FWD XLE. The 2026 Prius Nightshade starts at $34,300 or $35,700 with AWD, while the top-end Prius Limited starts at $37,065 with FWD and $38,465 with AWD. title: Don’t Build AI Governance From Scratch. Just Turn It On.
summary: Agent sprawl is growing. Here's how enterprise IT and security teams can govern AI at scale with the controls and visibility to stay ahead of the risk.
body_text: Every organization is in the middle of an agentic transformation. Teams everywhere are rapidly building and deploying agents that access data, trigger workflows, and influence decisions, often without centralized oversight. That shift happened fast. Faster than most organizations planned for. Gartner ® predicts that “by 2028, an average global Fortune 500 enterprise will have over 150,000 agents in use. Only 13% of organizations think they have the right AI agent governance in place.” The gap between those two numbers is where the risk lives. Agents are gaining more autonomy, coordinating across tools, handing off tasks, and executing multi-step processes with minimal human intervention. That autonomy raises the stakes: a single misconfiguration can pull customer PII into an unapproved workflow and cascade across systems before anyone notices, exposing customer data, inviting regulatory scrutiny, and eroding the trust your organization spent years building. For IT and security teams, the accountability falls to you. Atlassian helps you close that gap with AI governance built into the platform your teams already trust. The problem isn’t AI. It’s ungoverned AI. When AI adoption outpaces governance, three problems emerge: sensitive data becomes harder to control, agents begin to proliferate without consistent boundaries, and teams lose visibility into what AI systems are doing across the organization. This usually happens when AI is introduced outside the systems where work, permissions, and policies already live. Security teams are then left asking basic but critical questions: What’s running? Who created it? What can it access? What actions can it take? And when those answers are unclear, the default response is often to slow adoption. But long term, that creates a different kind of risk: teams still want AI, so they find workarounds that are even harder to govern. The better approach is to bring governance closer to the work itself. That means using AI that operates within the same platform, permissions model, and administrative controls your teams already trust. AI governance works better when it’s built into the Atlassian platform Atlassian has been the home for teamwork for over two decades. The projects, code, and institutional knowledge stored in the Atlassian Teamwork Graph provide the context that transforms generic AI output into outcomes that understand your project history, team structures, and strategic goals. Unlike vendors that require you to rebuild permissions, policies, and integrations from scratch, Atlassian’s AI, Rovo, runs on the same platform your teams already rely on. You do not need to recreate permissions, rebuild governance policies, or bolt on a separate administrative model just to start governing AI. The controls you already use for access, classification, and protection carry forward into AI experience. As agent usage expands, you can layer on agent-specific controls like scoped permissions, tool restrictions, and execution boundaries, without rearchitecting what’s already working. What AI governance looks like in practice Governing AI isn’t a single control or a checkbox. It is a connected system that helps you protect sensitive data, define what autonomous systems are allowed to do, and maintain visibility into what actually happened. At Atlassian, we think about AI governance in three parts: Securing the underlying data Setting boundaries for autonomous behavior Maintaining a record of everything that happened Each part matters on its own, but the model works best when all three operate together. Securing the underlying data AI security starts with data security. Before you scale AI across the organization, you need confidence in what data exists, how sensitive it is, where it lives, and who should be allowed to interact with it. For example, a contractor asks AI a question and the response includes source code from a repository they were never supposed to see. Or a summary pulls in compensation data and surfaces it in a shared channel. These aren’t edge cases. They’re the predictable result of using AI on unorganized, unclassified, or unmonitored data. Atlassian Guard gives security teams the controls to classify, monitor, and secure that foundation before AI ever touches it with: Content scanning – built-in and custom detections to discover what sensitive data already exists across your environment, and flag new risks in real time as users create content. Automatic classification – apply sensitivity labels based on rules your team defines, so there’s no ambiguity about what needs protecting or how to handle it. Org-level data security policies – block export, restrict sharing, and enforce protections at scale by mapping policies directly to your classification labels. Those controls cover your data foundation. The second layer of protection is specifically focused on your AI interactions, the data that can be pulled from external sources, and the surfaces where it appears. Rovo connector security scans third-party connector data in real-time and prevents sensitive content from entering our environment. Rovo Chat security scans user-level data to block or redact sensitive data from entering prompts and surfacing in responses. For organizations with stricter isolation, encryption, or sovereignty requirements, Atlassian also supports additional deployment and protection options, including Atlassian-hosted LLMs, customer-managed keys, and data residency choices. Together, these capabilities help extend your existing data security posture into AI without requiring a separate governance layer. Setting boundaries for autonomous behavior As more teams deploy autonomous AI, you need granular controls that adapt to your organization’s needs. Let’s look at another real-life scenario: a sales team deploys an agent to automate pipeline updates. It connects to your CRM, starts pulling customer contract data into a Confluence workflow you didn’t approve, and inherits full access permissions from the rep who built it last Tuesday. Each part of that scenario is avoidable when agents are governed with explicit boundaries from the start. Atlassian helps administrators set those boundaries through controls such as: Agent permissions – ensure that only teams approved to build agents can do so. Coming soon: agent identities – give every agent explicit, role-scoped access that can be audited and revoked independently. Set org-level defaults so every new agent is automatically scoped to the right apps and groups. MCP tool controls – govern which external systems agents can connect to, what actions they’re permitted to take, and require IDP verification through Okta before anyone connects via MCP, so access is controlled at the front door. And to make agent sprawl easier to manage, we’ve built a centralized console to view and manage every agent across your org. Coming soon : we’re adding the ability to take bulk actions to make managing agent sprawl even easier. When these controls live in the same administrative surface teams already use, governance becomes easier to operationalize. Instead of adding friction, it makes agent usage more consistent, more centralized, and easier to manage at scale. Maintaining a record of everything that happened Knowing what AI is authorized to do is one thing. Proving what it actually did is another. Imagine if your CISO asks, “An agent made a decision that affected a customer account. Can you tell me what it did, what data it used, and whether it followed policy?” To answer those questions, you need records, reporting, and operational visibility. Atlassian supports that visibility through capabilities such as: Audit logs – provide a traceable record of agent actions and what ran. Rovo insights – monitors AI activity across the organization, including which agents are running, how often, and who’s using them. Platform usage – tracks Rovo credit consumption across your organization so finance and IT can forecast spend, identify where AI is being used most, and make informed decisions about where to scale. And coming soon , the ROI calculator will help you answer whether the investment is paying off, with a clear picture of which agents are delivering results and which need attention. Together, these give you a continuous line of sight into adoption, compliance, and cost, not just after something goes wrong, but as a default operating posture. The road ahead The shift to agentic AI isn’t slowing down, and neither is the accountability that comes with it. But governance doesn’t have to be what slows you down. The organizations that will move fastest are the ones that use the foundations they’ve already built. If you’re not sure where your gaps are, that’s the place to start. title: Encouraging Growth Starts With Everyday Conversations
summary: Employee development is often associated with promotions, training programs or career milestones. But some of the most meaningful growth happens in everyday moments. It happens when a manager encourages an employee to ask questions. When someone is trusted with a new challenge. When feedback is shared with the intent to help someone improve. Those small interactions build […]
body_text: Employee development is often associated with promotions, training programs or career milestones. But some of the most meaningful growth happens in everyday moments. It happens when a manager encourages an employee to ask questions. When someone is trusted with a new challenge. When feedback is shared with the intent to help someone improve. Those small interactions build confidence, strengthen skills and create a culture where people continue learning throughout their careers. Gallup recognizes this in its sixth engagement element: There is someone at work who encourages my development. Employees who feel supported in their growth are more engaged, more likely to contribute ideas and more willing to take on new challenges. At Novanta, we see the impact of those conversations every day. One employee recently shared that having a manager who genuinely cares about his development has transformed his experience in his first full-time role. Rather than worrying about making mistakes, he feels empowered to ask questions, experiment with new approaches and continually look for better ways of working. That mindset benefits everyone. When employees know someone is invested in their success, they don’t just grow individually. They strengthen their teams, improve processes and help create an environment where innovation can thrive. As we continue growing across AI-driven robotics and automation, minimally invasive and robotic surgery, digital and AI-driven manufacturing, and precision medicine, our success depends on people who never stop learning. Development isn’t something that happens once a year. It’s built through consistent coaching, meaningful feedback and leaders who take the time to help others reach their potential. The question for all of us is simple: How can we encourage someone’s development today?

title: 2027 Mercedes-Maybach GLS 680 Pricing, Specs, and Release Date
summary: The Mercedes-Benz GLS lineup gets a refresh for 2027 which includes the Mercedes-Maybach version. Its name changes from GLS 600 to GLS 680 in the process, and the update includes design changes, more power, updated connected technology, and updated ADAS.
body_text: If the Mercedes-Benz name doesn’t carry enough cachet and luxury for you, the German luxury brand ups the ante with its line of Mercedes-Maybach models. The most comfortable for the most people among them is the new 2027 Mercedes-Maybach GLS 680, a full-size SUV meant to coddle occupants as they head to the country club. 2027 Mercedes-Maybach GLS 680 Pricing, Specs, and Release Date What’s New for the 2027 Mercedes-Maybach GLS 680 Design Powertrain Interior Technology Safety Pricing and Release Date Further Research What’s New for the 2027 Mercedes-Maybach GLS 680 Like the rest of the Mercedes-Benz GLS lineup, the Mercedes-Maybach GLS gets a refresh for 2027, changing its name from GLS 600 to GLS 680 in the process. The update includes design changes, more power, more sound deadening, updated connected technology, revised steering, a new trick for handling, and new driver-assistance and autonomous driving systems (ADAS). Design The Mercedes-Maybach GLS shares its basic design with the standard GLS but has several unique features. Up front, the grille features vertical ribs, sports the Maybach name along its top, and is illuminated at night. A Mercedes-Benz star logo hood ornament is a blast from the past. A black panel connects the grille to the headlights, which feature rose-gold accents, integrated Mercedes star lighting elements, and Mercedes’ Digital Light technology that uses more than a million facets and can dim light for oncoming drivers. A chrome surround frames the lower air intake. Along the sides, the GLS 680 has automatic retracting running boards with LED light strips. At the rear, Mercedes stars are integrated into the taillights to play off the front end, as does a chrome lower valance. Mercedes offers the GLS 680 with two-tone paint schemes. The GLS 680 comes standard with 22-inch wheels with a 20-hole design, and optional 23-inch forged wheels in the Mercedes monobloc design have the Mercedes-Benz star in their center mounted on a ball-bearing assembly that always keeps them upright. An optional Maybach Night Series Design package adds dark chrome trim to the exterior and comes with black and Black Pearl nappa leather or Crystal White nappa leather and Black Pearl accents. Also available are Beech Brown and Macchiato Beige Maybach Exclusive nappa leather and Grain Brown Walnut Wood and High-Gloss Silver Metallic Mixed Fabric trims. Inside, the GLS 680 features Mercedes’ Superscreen with three screens, including one for the front passenger. The driver display has Rose Gold dials. The air vents on the dash have a gondola design and are illuminated. Powertrain The Mercedes-Maybach GLS 680 comes with a single powertrain. It is a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 aided by a 48-volt mild hybrid system. Total output is 603 horsepower and 627 pound-feet of torque, increases of 53 hp and 89 lb-ft. The electric motor can add 23 hp to aid acceleration. Mercedes hasn’t said what the transmission is, but it’s likely the same nine-speed automatic as last year. Mercedes’ 4Matic all-wheel-drive (AWD) system comes standard, and the standard air suspension can raise and lower the ground clearance to clear obstacles or pull itself out of the mud in an Off-Road mode, but anyone who takes this ultra-luxury SUV off-roading will likely best be served by having their head examined. Fuel economy figures are not yet available, but the 2026 GLS 600 is EPA-rated at 13 mpg city, 18 highway, and 15 combined. Expect the same for the GLS 680. Interior If you can’t get comfortable in the GLS 680, you can’t get comfortable in any vehicle. Up front, it features the brand’s Multicontour seats with numerous power adjustments. The seats have a massage function, heating and ventilation. The Mercedes-Maybach GLS 680 seats only four, because it has the Executive Seats that recline and have calf rests. A massage function extends to those calf rests. A rear center console is standard, and it’s offered with an optional refrigerated compartment. Mercedes hasn’t shared cargo space figures, but they will certainly be compromised by the rear Executive Seats. The 2026 GLS 600 has just 18.4 cubic feet of space behind the second row. Technology The Mercedes-Maybach GLS 680 comes standard with the Mercedes-Benz Superscreen that includes 12.3-inch displays for the digital instrument cluster, center touchscreen, and a front passenger screen. The operating system uses artificial intelligence, is connected to the Mercedes-Benz Intelligent Cloud, and can keep current with over-the-air (OTA) updates. It has the MBUX Virtual Assistant that integrates ChapGPT, MicroSoft Bing search, and Google Gemini. The standard audio system is a 15-speaker Burmester unit with 710 watts of power, and an optional rear entertainment system adds a pair of rear 11.6-inch screens. All of the displays have Maybach-exclusive interfaces.
